name: Ruy Lopez
blurb: The Spanish: White puts the bishop on b5 to pressure the knight that defends e5. It leads to rich, slow middlegames and has been a top-level main line for over a century.

ideas.e4: Takes a central square and frees the queen and the f1 bishop.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3: Develops with an attack on the e5 pawn.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5: The bishop attacks the c6 knight, the piece defending e5. White is not threatening to win e5 yet, but the pressure lasts for many moves.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4: Keeps the bishop and its pressure on c6. Taking on c6 is also playable, but the retreat keeps more tension.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O: White castles and leaves e4 hanging on purpose. If Black takes it, d4 and Re1 open the centre while Black's king is still on e8.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1: The rook defends e4, so now White really does threaten Bxc6 followed by Nxe5.
The bishop steps back but keeps aiming at f7 along the diagonal.
Makes a retreat square on c2 for the bishop and prepares d4 to take more of the centre.
Stops ...Bg4, which would pin the f3 knight to the queen. Now d4 can follow without that pin.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4: After Black grabs e4, d4 attacks e5 and opens lines toward Black's king, which has not castled yet.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O: Against the Berlin, White castles and again leaves e4 undefended. If Black takes, White wins time with d4 against the uncastled king.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 d6 d4: Against the solid ...d6, White takes more space with d4 and asks Black how to hold e5.
